title: Hand Movements: A Window into Haptic Object Recognition

findings.antecedent: Haptic exploration of 3D objects for matching
findings.consequent: Overall mean percentage agreement (accuracy) in matching tasks
findings.mechanism: The haptic system can achieve high levels of perceptual performance for object recognition.

findings.antecedent: Type of Exploratory Procedure (Lateral Motion, Pressure, Static Contact, Unsupported Holding, Enclosure, Contour Following)
findings.mechanism: Different EPs inherently take different times to execute.
findings.quote: revealed significant effects of EP, F(5,50) = 33.3, p < .001

findings.antecedent: Type of instruction (desired object knowledge dimension: Texture, Hardness, Temperature, Weight, Volume, Global Shape, Exact Shape)
findings.mechanism: The overall duration of EPs was not significantly different across different instruction types.

findings.antecedent: Interaction between type of Exploratory Procedure (EP) and type of instruction (desired object knowledge dimension)
findings.mechanism: The specific EPs used varied significantly depending on the desired object knowledge.
findings.quote: and an interaction, F(30,300) = 29.9, p < .001. This indicates that EPs were not uniform over instructions.

findings.antecedent: Predicted EP/dimension links (e.g., lateral motion/texture, pressure/hardness)
findings.consequent: Observed EP durations (z-scores) during dimension-matching tasks
findings.mechanism: Hand movements are purposively related to desired object knowledge, supporting specific EP-dimension links.
findings.quote: This contrast was highly significant, F(1,300) = 97.31, p < .001. Thus, there is strong support for the EP/dimension pairings initially proposed.

findings.antecedent: Mean EP durations from first 5 observers vs. remaining 6 observers
findings.mechanism: Consistency in how different individuals perform exploratory procedures.
findings.quote: the intersubject reliability was very high, r(258) = .92, p < .0001.

findings.antecedent: Different haptic dimension-matching tasks (e.g., Hardness, Function, Global Shape, Part Motion, Temperature, Volume, Texture, Weight, Exact Shape)
findings.mechanism: Movement profiles are distinctive enough to identify the type of desired knowledge.
findings.quote: Cluster analysis of matching tasks on the basis of movement profiles.

findings.antecedent: Two scorers' identification of purposive exploration intervals
findings.mechanism: Consistency in identifying the start and end of purposive exploration.
findings.quote: Over nine randomly chosen trials, this value was 88%

findings.antecedent: Two scorers' classification of specific Exploratory Procedures (EPs)
findings.mechanism: Consistency in classifying specific exploratory procedures.
findings.quote: the percentage overlap in the durations of EPs scored in the same way by the two judges... was 86%.

findings.mechanism: Within the tested range, varying exploration duration did not systematically impact accuracy.
findings.quote: The effect on accuracy of altering the length of time that the observer was permitted to explore each object was quite variable, and no systematic trends were apparent.

findings.antecedent: Use of Contour Following Exploratory Procedure
findings.consequent: Above chance performance in matching objects based on exact shape
findings.mechanism: Contour following is the only EP that provides sufficient information for exact shape recognition.
findings.quote: It is contour following, which is necessary when matching objects on the basis of their exact shape.

findings.consequent: Above chance performance in dimension-matching tasks
findings.mechanism: Multiple EPs can sometimes provide enough information for a given dimension, but some are more effective than others.
findings.quote: There are from 1 to 6 EPs sufficient for each instruction, as shown in Fig. 3.

findings.antecedent: Use of the predicted Exploratory Procedure (EP) for a given dimension
findings.mechanism: The hand uses the most effective exploratory procedure for a given knowledge goal.
findings.quote: the highest accuracy scores tended to be those expected from the results of Experiment 1. In that sense, then, the predicted EP was usually optimal.

findings.mechanism: Pressure is the most effective EP for assessing hardness.
findings.quote: The predicted EPs were clear winners for the dimensions of pressure and temperature

findings.antecedent: Use of Static Contact Exploratory Procedure
findings.mechanism: Static contact is the most effective EP for assessing temperature.
findings.quote: The predicted EPs were clear winners for the dimensions of pressure and temperature

findings.antecedent: Use of Static Contact EP and Contour Following EP
findings.mechanism: These EPs are effective for global shape, contrary to initial prediction of enclosure.
findings.quote: static contact and contour following performed the global shape task best, although enclosure, the predicted EP, performed above chance.

findings.consequent: Specialization score (how much better an EP performs in its most successful condition vs. others)
findings.mechanism: Pressure is highly effective for a specific dimension (hardness) and less so for others.
findings.quote: Pressure proves to be the most highly specialized EP

findings.mechanism: Lateral motion is highly effective for a specific dimension (texture) and less so for others.
Enclosure is generally useful across many dimensions, but not a clear winner for any.
findings.quote: Enclosure is considerably less specialized than any of the other EPs. It is above chance for most dimensions, but not a clear winner for any.

stimuli.description: 36 sets of three-dimensional objects, each set with one standard and three comparison objects, varying across 9 dimensions (texture, hardness, temperature, weight, volume, general shape, exact shape, part motion, function).

limitations: Execution of one EP may inevitably involve another to some degree, potentially inflating the effectiveness of nonpredicted EPs.
Constraining EP execution by instructions may have reduced the effectiveness of some EPs (e.g., enclosure for global shape/volume).
Reliability scores for EP classification were lower than expected due to scoring rule development, suggesting potential for improvement in future studies.
